principle: Campus events are persistent institutional/world events with real sources or causes. They create participation context and schedule/obligation candidates without asserting attendance or inventing incidents for pacing.
rules: Event identity and cause/source exist independently of player observation.
Scheduled institutional events require scheduling authority and a source/calendar reference.
Emergent incidents require causal event provenance and incident-registration authority.
Crisis alerts require causal event provenance and alert authority.
Quiet periods are valid; no event is generated merely to improve pacing.
External participant entities must already exist before the event references them.
Every event requires a real compatible location and nonnegative finite capacity.
Mandatory/role-assigned events create obligation candidates but never prove attendance.
Optional events never auto-enroll or auto-attend the player.
NPC optional participation plans remain schedule/travel/capacity constrained.
Normal schedule conflicts remain explicit conflicts.
Crisis preemption requires both a permitting policy and authority with preempt_schedule scope.
Preemption output is a revision candidate, not a silent timetable mutation.
Institutional schedule-conflict outputs may become Step-14 justification candidates but are not self-approved excuses.
Cancellation requires provenance and competent authority and preserves event history.
Participation plan is not attendance; attendance is not interaction.
Step 15 directly mutates no relationship, wellbeing, academic record or year progression.
Academic enrichment remains Step 8-owned and should be referenced rather than duplicated.
